newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania opposition calls for Sunday demonstration.
newsitem.headline: Albania opposition calls for Sunday demonstration.

text.p: Albanian opposition parties called on Friday for a peaceful protest to protect citizens' rights and blamed the ruling Democratic Party of President Sali Berisha for the collapse of get-rich-quick investment schemes.

Three opposition parties -- the Socialists, centre-right Democratic Alliance and centre-left Social Democrats -- said they would organise a demonstration on Sunday in the main square of the capital, Tirana.

"To peacefully protest to protect the citizens' economic rights, (the opposition parties)...will organise a meeting at Skanderbeg Square on Sunday," said a joint statement published by the Socialist daily Zeri i popullit.
"The Socialist Party will support and lead the protection of people's interests, confronting the state with democratic action on a massive scale," a separate statement by the Socialists said.

Police remained stationed around Tirana to prevent a repeat of clashes on Wednesday when thousands of angry savers took to the streets to demand money back after one of the most popular schemes, run by a gypsy woman called Sude, collapsed.
Demonstrations spread beyond the capital on Thursday to the western city of Vlore and to Shkoder in the north, state media reported.
Small groups of protesters continued to gather outside the Tirana offices of pyramid scheme companies on Friday, but the tense atmosphere of the past days was absent.
The schemes, which lured thousands of Albanians into selling everything they owned with promises of big returns on small outlays, mushroomed after the fall of communism in 1990.
Three pyramid schemes have failed so far, leaving thousands out of pocket in Europe's poorest country. Four more have suspended payments to investors.
On Thursday the Albanian government ordered the seizure of 25.5 billion leks ($255 million) deposited by such schemes in state-owned banks.

But the opposition, which boycotted general elections last year claiming they were rigged by the Democrats, said the sequestration was a sign of the economic and institutional crisis within the state and repeated its call for new polls.
"The solution to the political and institutional crisis and economic collapse can be realised only through fresh elections," the Socialists' statement said.
